Pat Gunkel

One takes a tachistoscope, computer with a cathode ray tube (CRT), or a
movie and uses these to show a series of objects or scenes in variously
randomized sequence, say at a flicker rate or a variously randomly varying
rate, and observes. The things projected may be few in number, such as 2 or
3 scenes, repeated, or all different. The projection may go on for just
5 seconds or all day or for weeks. The set of things shown may or may not
be chosen for types of similarity or for greatest degree cr type of
heterogeneity or dissimilarity. Sequence randomization may or may not be
essential. Showing may be adjusted to the subject, say as to rate. Good
projection material would be a set of extremely complicated natural scenes.

Qne might specially randomize (say intrascenically) for successive location,
orientation, size, distortion, obscuration, complexity, &re. QGne may take
the rate of presentation up to the point where successive scenes blur or fuse,
in various respects at various rates. One might perform the experiment
with varying luminosity between or within presentations. One might fragment
the successive projectings so that fit is diachronic and like a jigsaw
puzzle. The subject might be acquainted with the aim of the experiment and
what to look for or at least not fail to note. One might wary the rate of
presentation in a gliding way, heterometrically. Etc.

There is an analogy to the Wiener method for using white noise to retrieve
cross-correlation kernels, or randomness to show form, what is in one way 4
perfect sampling. My method should in fact break reality or the process of
perception in half so as to show the edges or its important structure, which
is a structure by transformation or jintertransformation. The dimensions of
the world and perception should appear in native contrast for the first time.

seeing any such structure through the ends of analysis, as simply predictable,
